name: application-tabs
title: Tabs
description: Horizontal and vertical tab navigation components for switching between distinct content panels within the same page context, with base, icon, underline, pill, and vertical layout variants.
useWhen: Switching between two or more related content views that share the same page context, such as Overview and Settings.
Content sections are mutually exclusive — only one panel is visible at a time.
The number of tabs is between two and six; more than six tabs is better served by a dropdown or sidebar.
avoidWhen: The content under each tab is long enough that users would benefit from seeing multiple sections simultaneously — use a page with anchor links instead.
Tab labels are too long to fit horizontally on mobile — use a vertical tab layout or a select-based switcher.
The tabs represent sequential steps in a process — use a stepper component instead.
responsiveBehavior: Horizontal tab bars scroll horizontally on narrow viewports. Pill and underline variants maintain single-row layout. Vertical tabs remain in a side-by-side layout but may need to collapse to a dropdown on mobile.
accessibility: Use role='tablist', role='tab', and role='tabpanel' with aria-selected and aria-controls attributes to implement the ARIA Tabs pattern.
Arrow keys should move focus between tabs within the tablist; Tab key should move focus into the active panel.
Each tab panel must have an id matching the aria-controls value of its corresponding tab button.

variants.title: Base
variants.description: Standard horizontal tabs with a filled active indicator and plain text labels — the default choice for content panel switching.
accessibility: Active tab uses aria-selected='true'; inactive tabs use aria-selected='false'; focus moves with arrow keys.

variants.title: Base (Dark)
variants.description: Standard horizontal tabs adapted for dark application surfaces with dark tab bar background and light active indicator.
accessibility: Active tab and inactive tab label colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark tab bar backgrounds.

variants.title: With icons
variants.description: Horizontal tabs with an icon alongside each label for quicker visual identification of content sections.
accessibility: Icons are decorative when text labels are present; set aria-hidden='true' on icon elements.

variants.title: With icons (Dark)
variants.description: Icon-labeled horizontal tabs adapted for dark surfaces, maintaining icon and label legibility on dark backgrounds.
accessibility: Icon fill and label text must meet contrast requirements against dark tab backgrounds.

variants.title: Vertical
variants.description: Vertical tab list alongside a content panel, suited for settings pages or forms where many sections would overflow a horizontal row.
accessibility: Vertical tab lists use aria-orientation='vertical' on the tablist; up/down arrow keys navigate between tabs.

variants.title: Vertical (Dark)
variants.description: Vertical tab layout adapted for dark application surfaces, keeping the side panel and content area legible on dark backgrounds.
accessibility: Active tab highlight and tab label colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark sidebar backgrounds.

variants.title: Underline
variants.description: Minimal underline-style tabs where the active indicator is a bottom border rather than a filled background — a lighter visual treatment for content-heavy pages.
accessibility: Underline active indicator must be distinguishable without color alone — pair it with a color shift in the label text.

variants.title: Underline (Dark)
variants.description: Underline-style tabs adapted for dark surfaces, with the active underline visible against dark backgrounds.
accessibility: Underline color and active label text must meet contrast requirements on dark tab bars.

variants.title: Pills
variants.description: Pill-shaped tab buttons with rounded backgrounds on the active item — a softer style often used in filter bars, content type switchers, or marketing pages.
accessibility: Pill tabs follow the same ARIA tablist pattern; active pill background must contrast with both active and inactive label text.

variants.title: Pills (Dark)
variants.description: Pill-style tabs adapted for dark surfaces with the active pill background visible against dark tab bar backgrounds.
accessibility: Active pill background and label colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark application surfaces.
